findings.reason: it fixes the node's write paths to gc.py and process_liveness.py and makes the existing two walkers part of the same pass, instead of one more copy of one traversal.
findings.text: §2 asks for "a sweep that removes only files whose pid is not running... and prints each removal", which is the existing `garbage_collect`/`retention_sweep` contract with `--apply` and its printed removal list; the plan leaves the host module unnamed ("named in the manifest") and so invites a parallel sweep, when gc.py already carries two `/proc` walkers of its own — `_scratch_process_holders` (reckon/crew/gc.py:1071) and `_processes_holding` (reckon/crew/gc.py:1374) — and a third would be the fourth copy of the same traversal; liveness, including the zombie rule §2's "pid is not running" depends on, is owned by `process_alive` (reckon/crew/process_liveness.py:12) and `record_process_liveness` (reckon/crew/process_liveness.py:353), already imported by gc.py:57

findings.reason: the node brief must extend review_need's prompt and `Verdict` record with the outcome-vs-prediction pairing and reuse its threshold, rather than stand up a second Jev predictor beside it.
findings.text: §8's "Jev judgement of the probability that it finds a blocking defect is recorded on the review run's ledger row, with the inputs it was given" is the module that already exists: `review_need.judge` takes typed `Change` inputs plus goals, is thresholded by `review_need_threshold` (reckon/flight.py:1027), caches on the exact inputs, and is already called for a second-and-later run review at reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:1217 and for a plan review at reckon/crew/plan_review.py:1364; a second predictor with its own prompt, its own cached inputs and its own threshold view is the parallel mechanism the rubric exists to catch — the plan's write paths ("the picker module that calls Jev") do not name review_need.py at all

findings.reason: it names watch_unit.py and query.py as the row vocabulary's owners so the new kind is added once, in the set the reader parses.
findings.text: §5's "one row of its own kind" on the session's watch stream has an owner: `seat_moved_row` (reckon/crew/watch_unit.py:386) and `announce_seat_moved` (:429) write the existing kind, and the kind vocabulary is read back by `parse_watch_row` (reckon/crew/query.py:1362); the plan again defers the module ("the watch-row writer module (named in the manifest)"), so a worker may write rows directly from queue_admission.py and split the vocabulary between two writers and one reader

findings.reason: the section must extend the disposition owner and unify the kind vocabulary, or its "by hand is refused" assertion lands in a branch that a second writer bypasses.
findings.text: §4's new `deferred` kind must be added where finding dispositions are already owned, `review_dispositions.py` (writer at :481 and :572, "by the code path that does the deciding"), yet the plan's write paths name only queue_landing.py, findings.py and "the disposition CLI module"; the closed kind set is meanwhile already expressed in two unreconciled places — the dispatch in `finding_disposition` (reckon/crew/findings.py:223-229, kinds spelled inline as branches) and the sibling `DIMENSION_DISPOSITION_KINDS` tuple (reckon/crew/review.py:3941) — so "recording a `deferred` disposition by hand is refused" has no single place to be enforced, and the census is: findings.py:223, findings.py:226, review.py:3941, review_dispositions.py:481, review_dispositions.py:572

findings.reason: with one function returning a typed hold (kind + id) that dispatch, admission and the roadmap all render, §10 and §11 become one change in one place instead of edits to a dozen shallow call sites, and the plan's own done-when stops resting on cross-implementation agreement.
findings.text: §10's decision-scoped hold and §11's "name the hold" are the fourth and fifth dimensions of one decision that no module owns: the hold vocabulary is computed across queue_admission.py (17 sites), dispatch.py (3), runs.py (4), dispatch_batch.py (2), ticker.py (2), obligation_snapshot.py, mcp_views.py and node.py, and §10's done-when requires dispatch and admission to agree while §6 requires "queue admission and the launch-time check give the same answer" — a test asserting two implementations agree is the signature of a rule with no single owner

findings.reason: either drop the field and let §3's unconditional admit stand, or state what it still gates; as written it adds an accepted-and-inert option to the queue grammar the plan also refuses unknown fields against.
findings.text: §12 adds `allow_unreconciled_runs` to a batch entry that "is accepted and recorded on the request and has whatever effect the single-dispatch flag has", while §3 concurrently makes that flag change nothing (`--allow-unreconciled-runs` keeps parsing and changes nothing), so the field carries a waiver no longer honoured — surface that exists only to mirror a retired behaviour

findings.reason: each of the six must account in its own text for the surface it adds, and §3's retention of `--allow-unreconciled-runs` beside §12's copy of it is the one retirement the plan could take and does not.
findings.text: measured against public_definitions 2506, cli_options 473, mcp_views 15, refusal_families 25: §2 adds a sweep entry point and §4 a disposition kind plus a new refusal family, §5 a watch-row kind, §8 a view (mcp_views 15→16), §12 two batch fields (cli_options family) and §14 a new `edit_plan` verb that must be served in the documented op grammar (`op_vocab`, reckon/mcp_edit_plan.py:1504) — six sections adding to four of the four families, and none of the six names what it retires or merges, or says why nothing can be

findings.reason: the brief must name mcp_edit_plan.py as the verb and grammar owner, or the new op is invisible to every caller that reads op_vocab.
findings.text: §14's write paths name `reckon/mcp.py` and `reckon/_store.py` for a new `edit_plan` verb, but the op vocabulary, its dispatcher and its served grammar live in `reckon/mcp_edit_plan.py` (`Verbs (the "op" key): set | append | resolve | lock | accept | gate | pass | fail | retire_prose | move` at :1504, and the `op_vocab` the tool returns to clients), so a node briefed from these paths adds a verb the served grammar does not carry and the plan's own "in one versioned write" is never assembled
